summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple sclerosis and a chronic suprapubic catheter, was admitted for fatigue and gross hematuria. He had leukocytosis and a positive urinalysis, prompting treatment for a complicated urinary tract infection. Empiric vancomycin and cefepime were started, then adjusted to meropenem due to rising white count and history of resistant organisms like Providencia. The initial urine culture was contaminated, and subsequent cultures were sterilized by antibiotics. His treatment was narrowed to cefepime and then transitioned to oral clindamycin. A midline catheter was placed for IV access, but home infusion was denied, so he completed therapy inpatient. Dental evaluation revealed parotitis and periapical abscesses; he was discharged on clindamycin for dental infection and with dental follow-up planned. His catheter was replaced during admission. He improved clinically and was discharged home in stable condition.
